seo.shortDescription: Searchable 2026 U.S. tariff table for all 421 HTS Chapter 90 lines — medical devices, syringes, implants, hearing aids, X-ray and lab instruments, lenses, eyeglasses, cameras and measuring equipment. Base rates Free to 16%, plus the extra duty by country: Section 301, China lists, Section 232 and Canada Section 338.
keywords: tariffs on medical devices from china

overview.intro:
Chapter 90 covers optical, photographic, measuring, precision and medical instruments: lenses and optical fibers, eyeglasses and sunglasses, cameras and microscopes, surveying and navigation instruments, lab analyzers, meters, test and inspection equipment, thermostats — and the largest group, **medical, surgical, dental and orthopedic devices**, from syringes and catheters to implants, hearing aids, ultrasound, MRI and X-ray. Base rates are low: 308 of the 421 lines are Free, including every medical and orthopedic line, and the dutiable ones pay mostly 1%–7% (16% at most, on rifle-scope parts).

The U.S. imported **$125.68B** of Chapter 90 goods in 2025, 35% of it medical instruments of heading 9018 ($44.52B) and 15% orthopedic devices and implants ($19.41B). **Mexico** ($24.14B), **Germany** ($13.53B), **China** ($10.23B) and **Ireland** ($9.89B) are the largest suppliers, followed by Costa Rica and Japan. Because the base rates are low, the duty you pay is mostly the **extra duty by country**: since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff — 10% in total for the EU, 12.5% for Japan, Korea and Switzerland, +12.5% for Costa Rica and Singapore. **China adds 37.5%** on most instruments and imaging equipment and **112.5% on syringes and needles**. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico and Canada pay nothing, and 63 British medical-device lines are exempt. A **Section 232 investigation of medical devices** has been open since September 2025 but has imposed no duty.

stats.label: Lines with an extra duty for some origins
stats.note: Section 301 (2026, 60 economies): 411 (not the 10 semiconductor-equipment lines on the note 52(b) list); Brazil: 421; China Lists 1–4A: 364; China 2024 increase (100%, syringes and needles): 4; Canada Section 338: 1 (also on USMCA goods); Section 232 vehicle parts: 5 (only when they are car, truck or bus parts); Section 232 metals: 1; Russia: 8 lines at 35% in lieu of column 2 and 2 at 200% on aluminum

productGroups.label: Optical fibers, contact lenses, spectacle lenses & unmounted optics
productGroups.blurb: Optical fibers, fiber bundles and fiber cables not of heading 8544 pay 6.7%; contact lenses and spectacle lenses 2%; polarizing sheets and unmounted lenses, prisms and mirrors enter Free.

productGroups.label: Mounted lenses, filters, prisms & mirrors for instruments
productGroups.blurb: Mounted lenses and other optical elements that are parts of instruments: projection lenses 2.45%, other camera objective lenses 2.3%; CCTV camera lenses, filters, mounted prisms and mirrors enter Free.

productGroups.label: Eyeglass frames & parts
productGroups.blurb: Plastic spectacle frames and frame parts pay 2.5%; frames of metal and other materials enter Free.

productGroups.label: Sunglasses, safety glasses & goggles
productGroups.blurb: Sunglasses pay 2%; safety glasses, safety goggles, swimming goggles and other spectacles 2.5%. Finished corrective eyeglasses are classified here too.

productGroups.label: Binoculars, telescopes & astronomical instruments
productGroups.blurb: Prism binoculars enter Free; optical telescopes and monoculars pay 8%, other astronomical instruments 6%. Parts and accessories pay "the rate applicable to the article of which they are a part" — the importer names that article (see below).
productGroups.rateSummary: Free · 8% · 6% · The rate applicable to the article of which it is a part or accessory

productGroups.label: Still cameras, flash units & parts
productGroups.blurb: Most film cameras — SLR, 35 mm, instant-print and other cameras valued over $10 — and flash units enter Free; instant and other cameras valued $10 or less pay 6.8%, some fixed-focus and roll-film cameras 4%; camera parts 5.8%, other parts 3.9%. Digital cameras are not here (heading 8525).

productGroups.label: Cinematographic cameras & projectors
productGroups.blurb: Cinematographic cameras enter Free; cine projectors Free to 4.9%; parts and accessories Free to 3.9%.

productGroups.label: Image projectors, enlargers & reducers
productGroups.blurb: Slide projectors pay 7%, other image projectors 4.6%; microform readers 3.5%, or Free if they can make copies; enlargers and reducers Free; parts Free or 2.9%. Video and data projectors are not here (heading 8528).

productGroups.label: Photo lab equipment, negatoscopes & projection screens
productGroups.blurb: Automatic film processors pay 2.4%; most other darkroom apparatus, negatoscopes and projection screens enter Free; some parts 2.9%.

productGroups.label: Optical microscopes
productGroups.blurb: Compound optical microscopes enter Free; stereoscopic microscopes with a camera pay 3.9% and other stereo microscopes 7.2%; parts Free.

productGroups.label: Electron microscopes & diffraction apparatus
productGroups.blurb: Electron and other non-optical microscopes and diffraction apparatus, and their parts, enter Free.

productGroups.label: Lasers, rifle scopes, magnifiers & other optical devices
productGroups.blurb: Lasers (other than laser diodes) enter Free. Telescopic sights for rifles pay 14.9% (1.4% if designed for infrared light) and their parts 16%; periscopes and similar 5.3%; magnifiers and loupes 6.6%; door viewers 5.8%; other optical devices and other parts 4.5%. 9013.90.80 parts are also a Section 232 derivative article (15% in total).

productGroups.label: Compasses, autopilots & navigational instruments
productGroups.blurb: Compasses, gyrocompasses, autopilots, ship logs, depth sounders and other navigational instruments, and their parts, enter Free. Radar and GPS receivers are in heading 8526.

productGroups.label: Surveying, rangefinders, weather & geophysical instruments
productGroups.blurb: Rangefinders, theodolites, total stations, levels, photogrammetric, weather and geophysical instruments enter Free, except non-electrical levels (2.8%). Rangefinders of 9015.10 can carry the Section 232 auto-parts duty when they are car parts.

productGroups.label: Precision balances (5 cg or better)
productGroups.blurb: Balances with a sensitivity of 5 cg or better: electrical 3.9%, jewelers' 2.9%, other 3.3%, including parts.

productGroups.label: Drafting instruments, calipers, micrometers & measuring tapes
productGroups.blurb: Plotters enter Free; other drafting machines, slide rules and calculating instruments 3.9%; other drawing and marking-out instruments 4.6%; micrometers and calipers 5.8%, other gauges 3.9%; other hand measuring instruments such as rulers and tape measures 5.3%. Parts take the rate of the article they belong to.
productGroups.rateSummary: Free · 3.9% · 4.6% · 5.8% · 5.3% · The rate applicable to the article of which it is a part or accessory

productGroups.label: Medical, surgical, dental & veterinary instruments (incl. syringes, catheters, ECG, ultrasound, MRI)
productGroups.blurb: All medical, surgical, dental and veterinary instruments enter Free: ECG, ultrasound, MRI and patient monitors, syringes and needles, catheters and cannulas, dental drills and burs, ophthalmic instruments, surgical instruments, defibrillators and dialysis apparatus. The extra duty depends on origin: Chinese syringes and needles pay 100% more under Section 301.

productGroups.label: Massage & mechano-therapy apparatus, oxygen therapy, ventilators & CPAP
productGroups.blurb: Massage apparatus, mechano-therapy appliances, oxygen and aerosol therapy apparatus, ventilators, CPAP machines and nebulizers enter Free.

productGroups.label: Breathing appliances & gas masks
productGroups.blurb: Gas masks and breathing appliances with mechanical parts or replaceable filters pay 2.5%; complete underwater breathing devices Free. Plain protective masks without filters are classified by material.

productGroups.label: Orthopedic devices, implants, artificial joints, hearing aids & pacemakers
productGroups.blurb: All orthopedic and implant devices enter Free: bone plates and screws, braces and splints, artificial joints, dental implants and teeth, other prosthetics, hearing aids, pacemakers and other implanted devices.

productGroups.label: X-ray, CT & radiotherapy apparatus and X-ray tubes
productGroups.blurb: X-ray, CT, dental X-ray and radiotherapy apparatus, X-ray tubes and ionization smoke detectors enter Free; generators, beam-delivery units and parts pay 0.8%–1.4%.

productGroups.label: Demonstration instruments & models
productGroups.blurb: Instruments, apparatus and models designed only for demonstration in education or exhibitions enter Free.

productGroups.label: Materials-testing machines (hardness, strength)
productGroups.blurb: Machines and appliances for testing the hardness, strength, compressibility or elasticity of materials, and their parts, enter Free.

productGroups.label: Thermometers, pyrometers, barometers, hydrometers & hygrometers
productGroups.blurb: Thermometers and pyrometers — liquid-filled, digital and infrared — enter Free, as do their parts; other electrical instruments such as electronic hygrometers 1.7%; barometers 1%, hydrometers 2.9%, hygrometers 1.4%, recording instruments 1%, others 1.6%.

productGroups.label: Flow meters, level gauges & pressure instruments
productGroups.blurb: Flow meters, level gauges, pressure gauges and transmitters, heat meters and their parts enter Free.

productGroups.label: Laboratory analysis instruments: spectrometers, chromatographs, analyzers
productGroups.blurb: Spectrometers, chromatographs, gas and smoke analyzers, mass spectrometers, NMR instruments, microtomes and their parts enter Free; exposure meters 1.2%.

productGroups.label: Gas, liquid & electricity supply meters
productGroups.blurb: Gas meters and liquid (water) meters pay 16¢ each + 2.5%; electricity meters and parts enter Free.

productGroups.label: Counters, taximeters, speedometers & tachometers
productGroups.blurb: Speedometers, tachometers, odometers and production counters enter Free; taximeters 5.3%, bicycle speedometers 6%, stroboscopes 16¢ each + 2.5%. Revolution counters and speedometers can carry the Section 232 auto-parts or truck-parts duty when they are vehicle parts.

productGroups.label: Oscilloscopes, multimeters, electrical test & radiation-measuring instruments
productGroups.blurb: Oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, multimeters, network analyzers, semiconductor-wafer testers and radiation detectors enter Free; resistance-measuring instruments without a recorder 1.7%.

productGroups.label: Measuring & inspection machines: CMMs, wafer and mask inspection, test benches
productGroups.blurb: Balancing machines, coordinate-measuring machines, optical inspection systems including wafer, photomask and reticle inspection, and other measuring instruments enter Free; test benches 1.7%. Ten semiconductor-related lines are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty.

productGroups.label: Thermostats, manostats & automatic regulating instruments
productGroups.blurb: Thermostats pay 1.7%; manostats and hydraulic or pneumatic regulators Free; voltage regulators for 6, 12 or 24 V systems 1.1%; other automatic regulating and control instruments and parts 1.7%.

productGroups.label: Parts & accessories not specified elsewhere in Chapter 90
productGroups.blurb: Parts and accessories not covered elsewhere in the chapter: LED backlight modules and touch screens without display enter Free, other parts 4.4%.

rateTable.note: Rates shown in grey are inherited from the parent heading. HTSUS states a duty once on the 8-digit line and leaves the 10-digit statistical lines blank; this table resolves each line to the rate that actually applies to it.

workedExamples.title: Disposable syringes from China
workedExamples.body: Hypodermic syringes are Free. China adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) and +100% under the 2024 Section 301 increase (9903.91.03): **112.5%**, $11,250 on a $10,000 order. The same syringes pay 10% from Malaysia, India or the UK, 10% in total from the EU, and nothing from Mexico under USMCA.

workedExamples.title: Artificial hip joints from Ireland
workedExamples.body: Artificial joints are Free. As an EU product with a base rate under 10%, they pay **10% in total** (9903.05.39): $10,000 on a $100,000 shipment. From Switzerland 12.5% in total; from China 12.5% (9021.31 is on no China list); from the UK **Free**, because artificial joints are on the UK exception list (note 52(j)(1)); from Mexico Free under USMCA.

workedExamples.title: Catheters from Costa Rica
workedExamples.body: Catheters and cannulas are Free. Costa Rica pays +12.5% (9903.05.33), which CAFTA-DR does not remove: **12.5%**, $12,500 on $100,000. The Dominican Republic also pays 12.5%, India 10%, and USMCA-qualifying catheters from Mexico nothing.

workedExamples.title: Telescope parts from China or Germany
workedExamples.body: Parts of telescopes pay "the rate applicable to the article of which it is a part": for a part of an optical telescope (9005.80.40) that is **8%**. The importer gives the article's line, and the calculator prices the part at 8% of its value. China adds 12.5% plus 7.5% (List 4A on 9005.90): **28%**. From Germany the EU rule gives the higher of 10% and the 8%: **10%** in total.

workedExamples.title: Optical measuring instrument from Canada
workedExamples.body: Other optical measuring and checking instruments are Free. Canadian ones pay the **50% Section 338 duty** (9903.03.14) even when USMCA-qualifying — $5,000 on $10,000 — and 60% if not USMCA-qualifying. From Mexico under USMCA they pay nothing, from Germany 10% in total, from China 37.5% (List 1).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover: (a) articles of a kind used in machines, appliances or for other technical uses, of vulcanized rubber other than hard rubber (heading 4016), of leather or of composition leather (heading 4205) or of textile material (heading 5911); (b) supporting belts or other support articles of textile material, whose intended effect on the organ to be supported or held derives solely from their elasticity (for example, maternity belts, thoracic support bandages, abdominal support bandages, supports for joints or muscles) (section XI); (c) refractory goods of heading 6903; ceramic wares for laboratory, chemical or other technical uses, of heading 6909; (d) glass mirrors, not optically worked, of heading 7009, or mirrors of base metal or of precious metal, not being optical elements (heading 8306 or chapter 71); (e) goods of heading 7007, 7008, 7011, 7014, 7015 or 7017; (f) parts of general use, as defined in note 2 to section XV, of base metal (section XV) or similar goods of plastics (chapter 39); however, articles specially designed for use exclusively in implants in medical, surgical, dental or veterinary sciences are to be classified in heading 9021; (g) pumps incorporating measuring devices, of heading 8413; weight-operated counting or checking machinery, or separately entered weights for balances (heading 8423); lifting or handling machinery (headings 8425 to 8428); paper or paperboard cutting machines of all kinds (heading 8441); fittings for adjusting work or tools on machine tools or water-jet cutting machines, of heading 8466, including fittings with optical devices for reading the scale (for example, "optical" dividing heads) but not those which are in themselves essentially optical instruments (for example, alignment telescopes); calculating machines (heading 8470); valves or other appliances of heading 8481, machines and apparatus (including apparatus for the projection or drawing of circuit patterns on sensitized semiconductor materials) of heading 8486; (h) searchlights or spotlights of a kind used for cycles or motor vehicles (heading 8512); portable electric lamps of heading 8513; cinematographic sound recording, reproducing or re-recording apparatus (heading 8519); sound-heads (heading 8522); television cameras, digital cameras and video camera recorders (heading 8525); radar apparatus, radio navigational aid apparatus and radio remote control apparatus (heading 8526); connectors for optical fibers, optical fiber bundles and cables (heading 8536); numerical control apparatus (heading 8537); sealed beam lamp units of heading 8539; optical fiber cables of heading 8544; (ij) searchlights or spotlights of heading 9405; (k) articles of chapter 95; (l) monopods, bipods, tripods and similar articles, of heading 9620; (m) capacity measures, which are to be classified according to their constituent material; or (n) spools, reels or similar supports (which are to be classified according to their constituent material, for example, in heading 3923 or section XV).

**Note 2.** Subject to note 1 above, parts and accessories for machines, apparatus, instruments or articles of this chapter are to be classified according to the following rules: (a) parts and accessories which are goods included in any of the headings of this chapter or of chapter 84, 85 or 91 (other than heading 8487, 8548 or 9033) are in all cases to be classified in their respective headings; (b) other parts and accessories, if suitable for use solely or principally with a particular kind of machine, instrument or apparatus, or with a number of machines, instruments or apparatus of the same heading (including a machine, instrument or apparatus of heading 9010, 9013 or 9031) are to be classified with the machines, instruments or apparatus of that kind; (c) all other parts and accessories are to be classified in heading 9033.

**Note 3.** The provisions of notes 3 and 4 to section XVI apply also to this chapter.

**Note 4.** Heading 9005 does not apply to telescopic sights for fitting to arms, periscopic telescopes for fitting to submarines or tanks, or to telescopes for machines, appliances, instruments or apparatus of this chapter or section XVI; such telescopic sights and telescopes are to be classified in heading 9013.

**Note 5.** Measuring or checking optical instruments, appliances or machines which, but for this note, could be classified both in heading 9013 and in heading 9031 are to be classified in heading 9031.

**Note 6.** For the purposes of heading 9021, the expression "orthopedic appliances" means appliances for: (a) preventing or correcting bodily deformities; or (b) supporting or holding parts of the body following an illness, operation or injury. Orthopedic appliances include footwear and special insoles designed to correct orthopedic conditions, provided that they are either (1) made to measure or (2) mass-produced, entered singly and not in pairs and designed to fit either foot equally.

**Note 7.** Heading 9032 applies only to: (a) instruments and apparatus for automatically controlling the flow, level, pressure or other variables of liquids or gases, or for automatically controlling temperature, whether or not their operation depends on an electrical phenomenon which varies according to the factor to be automatically controlled, which are designed to bring this factor to, and maintain it at, a desired value, stabilized against disturbances, by constantly or periodically measuring its actual value; and (b) automatic regulators of electrical quantities, and instruments or apparatus for automatically controlling non-electrical quantities the operation of which depends on an electrical phenomenon varying according to the factor to be controlled, which are designed to bring this factor to, and maintain it at, a desired value, stabilized against disturbances, by constantly or periodically measuring its actual value.
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**1.** For the purposes of headings 9001 and 9002, the term "optically worked" refers to glass the surface of which has been ground or polished in order to produce the required optical properties.

**2.** For the purposes of this chapter, the term "electrical" when used in reference to instruments, appliances, apparatus and machines, refers to those articles the operation of which depends on an electrical phenomenon which varies according to the factor to be ascertained.

**3.** For the purposes of this chapter, the terms "optical appliances" and "optical instruments" refer only to those appliances and instruments which incorporate one or more optical elements, but do not include any appliances or instruments in which the incorporated optical element or elements are solely for viewing a scale or for some other subsidiary purpose.

**4.** For the purposes of this chapter, the term "printed circuit assembly" means goods consisting of one or more printed circuits of heading 8534 with one or more active elements assembled thereon, with or without passive elements. For the purposes of this note, "active elements" means diodes, transistors and similar semiconductor devices, whether or not photosensitive, of heading 8541, and integrated circuits of heading 8542.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 90: Optical, Medical & Precision Instruments — Tariff Updates

seo.title: HTS Chapter 90 Tariff Updates 2026: Medical Device, Optical & Instrument Duties Since January 2025 | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What changed for HTS Chapter 90 — medical devices, syringes, implants, X-ray, lab and measuring instruments, lenses and eyeglasses — since January 2025: the end of the IEEPA and Section 122 duties, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs, the 100% China duty on syringes and needles, Section 232 auto parts and metals, the pending Section 232 medical-device investigation and Canada Section 338, with Federal Register citations.
keywords: tariffs on medical devices from china

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). **No Chapter 90 base rate changed** and no line was added or renumbered: medical, surgical, dental and orthopedic devices are still Free, and most instruments pay Free to about 7%.

Everything that changed sits on top of the base rate. In 2025 the IEEPA duties reached medical devices and instruments from almost every country — up to 145% extra for China in April–May 2025, 15% in total for the EU and Japan from August 2025. They **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff**: +10% (Mexico and Canada unless USMCA, Malaysia, India, the UK), +12.5% (Costa Rica, Singapore, Israel, Vietnam, China), 10% in total for the EU and Taiwan, 12.5% for Japan, Korea and Switzerland. Ten semiconductor-equipment measuring lines are exempt, and so are 63 British medical-device lines. China also keeps its 2018–2019 lists (**+25%** on most imaging, analytical and measuring instruments, **+7.5%** on lenses, frames, sunglasses, binoculars and cameras) and, since September 27, 2024, **+100% on syringes and needles**. Two kinds of **Section 232** duty reach the chapter: vehicle-parts duties on rangefinders, speedometers and counters that are car or truck parts, and since April 6, 2026 a 15%-in-total metals duty on 9013.90.80 optical parts. A **Section 232 investigation of medical devices, consumables and PPE**, opened September 2, 2025, has not led to any duty. Since August 22, 2026 Canadian optical measuring instruments of 9031.49.90 pay a **50% Section 338 duty**, even under USMCA. No antidumping or countervailing duty order names a Chapter 90 product.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 90 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exemptions (notes 52(b), 52(d), 52(j)), the Brazil Section 301 tariff, the China Section 301 Lists 1, 2, 3 and 4A, the 2024 China increases and the product exclusions, the Section 232 duties on automobile parts, medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts and steel, aluminum and copper derivatives, the 200% duty on Russian aluminum, the Canada Section 338 duties, Russia's rates in lieu of column 2, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. Pending: the Section 232 investigation of medical equipment and devices, and the Section 232 semiconductor action, which so far charges no Chapter 90 line. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.whatItMeans: A car speedometer from Mexico (non-USMCA), Malaysia or India pays 25%; from Japan or the EU 15% in total; from China 50% with List 2.

inEffect.measure: Section 232 medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts
inEffect.exemption: Covers 2 Chapter 90 lines on the U.S. note 38(i) list: other counters and odometers (9029.10.80) and speedometers and tachometers (9029.20.40.80) — when they are parts of medium- and heavy-duty trucks, tractors or buses. USMCA-qualifying parts enter under 9903.74.10 and articles that are not such parts under 9903.74.11. A part of a passenger vehicle or light truck pays the automobile-parts duty instead. There is no deal rate for the UK, EU, Japan, Korea or Taiwan. Exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(f)).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A truck speedometer pays 25% from Germany, Japan, Mexico (non-USMCA) or Korea, and 50% from China (with List 2); a USMCA-qualifying one pays nothing.

changes.title: No Chapter 90 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 421 Chapter 90 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition, and no line was added or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 lists continue after the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR announced that the 2018 China Section 301 actions did not terminate on their 2026 anniversaries because domestic industries asked for them to continue. For Chapter 90 this keeps +25% (Lists 1, 2 and 3) on most medical imaging, analytical, measuring and optical goods and +7.5% (List 4A) on lenses, frames, sunglasses, binoculars and cameras.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 lists revised; Chapter 90 entry unchanged
changes.detail: Proclamations 11064 and 11065 added and removed provisions on the 9903.03.12 and 9903.03.14 lists and made the 50% apply in addition to any Section 232 duty. 9031.49.90 stays on the list, no other Chapter 90 provision was added, and the September 29, 2026 Canadian import bans name no Chapter 90 product.

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty reaches optical measuring instruments
changes.detail: 50% on listed products of Canada after a 3-day suspension lapsed. Chapter 90 is on the 9903.03.14 list with one subheading: other optical instruments and appliances for measuring or checking (9031.49.90). Unlike the Section 301 duty, it applies to USMCA-qualifying goods too (U.S. note 51(a)).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies cover almost all of Chapter 90
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84), reaching 411 of 421 lines. The general exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86) takes out 10 semiconductor-related lines: instruments for measuring or checking semiconductor wafers or devices (9030.82), optical inspection of wafers, photomasks and reticles (9031.41), mask inspection (9031.49.70), electron-beam measuring microscopes (9031.80.40) and their parts. EU and Taiwan goods pay 10% in total, Japan, Korea and Switzerland 12.5%. The UK exception list (note 52(j)(1)) exempts 63 British medical-device lines. Civil aircraft articles (note 52(d)), vehicle parts and metals that pay Section 232 (note 52(f)) and USMCA-qualifying goods (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94) are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 90 line is on the Brazil exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)); civil aircraft articles and goods that pay Section 232 are exempt. From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 tariff (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still remove the base rate, the Section 301 duty and the Section 232 vehicle-parts duties on qualifying Mexican and Canadian medical devices and instruments.

changes.title: Taiwan: Section 232 auto parts capped at 15% in total
changes.detail: Taiwanese rangefinders, counters and speedometers that are car or light-truck parts pay 15% in total in place of the base rate and the 25% duty (9903.94.67).

changes.title: Scheduled: metals duty on 9013.90.80 optical parts rises to 25% in 2028
changes.detail: From January 1, 2028 the temporary 15%-in-total rate for fixed industrial equipment derivatives ends: 9013.90.80 will pay the base rate + 25% (9903.82.09), 15% for UK goods with UK-smelted or cast aluminum (9903.82.05) and 10% with U.S.-smelted aluminum (9903.82.06) (Proclamation 11021, clause 7).

changes.title: Section 232 metals duty on 9013.90.80 optical parts: 15% in total
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 rebuilt the Section 232 metals duties on the full customs value and listed 9013.90.80 (other parts and accessories of lasers and other optical appliances) among the fixed industrial equipment derivatives of U.S. note 16(c)(ix): 15% in total until December 31, 2027 (9903.82.10), 10% in total with at least 85% U.S.-smelted and cast aluminum (9903.82.07), base rate + 25% for column 2 countries (9903.82.12). Goods with no aluminum, steel or copper, or less than 15% metal by weight, are outside it (9903.82.01, 9903.82.03). The same proclamation ended the general aluminum-content duty on 9031.90.91 parts (except Russian aluminum).

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 90 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03); civil aircraft articles were relieved (9903.03.05). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico and goods paying Section 232 were exempt.

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. The 25% reciprocal rate on India ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: AGOA reauthorized through December 31, 2026
changes.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (P.L. 119-75) renewed AGOA retroactively from September 30, 2025. AGOA (SPI D) makes the dutiable Chapter 90 lines Free for eligible sub-Saharan countries. GSP (SPI A, A*, A+), printed on most dutiable Chapter 90 lines, remains expired since December 31, 2020.

changes.title: Section 232 semiconductor action: no Chapter 90 line charged
changes.detail: Proclamation 11002 found that imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and their derivatives threaten national security. It put a 25% duty (U.S. note 39, 9903.79.01) only on certain advanced logic chips and products containing them, classified in 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30, and ordered negotiations on the rest; it said broader tariffs on semiconductor manufacturing equipment may follow. No Chapter 90 line — including the wafer and mask inspection equipment of 9031.41 — is on the note 39 list.

changes.title: Scheduled: Section 301 tariff on products of Nicaragua
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that pay the column 1-general rate (that is, not entered under CAFTA-DR) will pay +10% (9903.89.01) from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028. Today Nicaragua pays the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.58).

changes.title: China Section 301 exclusions for about 20 Chapter 90 products extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended 178 China Section 301 product exclusions through November 9, 2026 (U.S. note 20(vvv), 9903.88.69). In Chapter 90 they include disposable ECG electrodes, portable ultrasonic scanners, blood-pressure monitors, peak-flow meters and fingertip pulse oximeters for professional use, anesthesia instruments, electrosurgical cautery pencils, PET/CT scanners, radiotherapy systems, X-ray tube housings, multi-leaf collimators, certain clinical thermometers and gas monitors, protective goggles, prism binoculars, weather station sets and wall thermostats. Matching goods skip the List 1, 2, 3 or 4A duty; the 2026 duty still applies.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: South Korea: Section 232 auto parts capped at 15% in total
changes.detail: Korean rangefinders, counters and speedometers that are car or light-truck parts pay 15% in total (9903.94.63), retroactive to November 1, 2025, under the notice published December 4, 2025.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on truck and bus speedometers and counters
changes.detail: 25% on parts of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles listed in U.S. note 38(i) (9903.74.08), from every country with no deal rate: in Chapter 90, other revolution counters and odometers (9029.10.80) and speedometers and tachometers (9029.20.40.80). USMCA-qualifying parts are exempt (9903.74.10).

changes.title: Section 232 investigation of medical equipment, devices, consumables and PPE
changes.detail: Commerce opened a national security investigation on September 2, 2025 into imports of personal protective equipment, medical consumables (for example syringes, needles, catheters, infusion pumps, surgical instruments and anesthesia equipment) and medical equipment and devices (for example pacemakers, insulin pumps, stents, heart valves, hearing aids, prosthetics, orthopedic appliances, glucose monitors, CT and MRI scanners, X-ray, electrosurgical and respiratory apparatus) — most of headings 9018–9022. Comments were due October 17, 2025. As of October 13, 2026 no proclamation has imposed a duty under it.

changes.title: Japan: Section 232 auto parts capped at 15% in total
changes.detail: Japanese rangefinders, counters and speedometers that are car or light-truck parts pay 15% in total in place of the base rate and the 25% duty (9903.94.43).

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84), on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian medical devices and instruments, on top of the base rate. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set country rates for goods entered from August 7, 2025: Malaysia and Thailand +19%, Vietnam and Taiwan +20%, India +25%, Switzerland +39%, the UK +10%. EU goods with a column 1 rate under 15% paid 15% in total (9903.02.20) — so German or Irish medical devices paid 15%. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: EU: Section 232 auto parts capped at 15% in total
changes.detail: EU rangefinders, counters and speedometers that are car or light-truck parts pay 15% in total (9903.94.53), retroactive to August 1, 2025, under the notice published September 25, 2025.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: UK: Section 232 auto parts at 10% in total
changes.detail: British rangefinders (9015.10.40.00, 9015.10.80.00), counters (9029.10.40.00, 9029.10.80.00) and speedometers (9029.20.40.80), all on the UK list in note 33(j), pay 10% in total (9903.94.32) when they are car parts.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10% for goods entered from May 14, 2025. A Chinese patient monitor (Free, List 1) then paid 25% + 20% + 10% = 55% until November 9, 2025. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on automobile parts reaches rangefinders, counters and speedometers
changes.detail: 25% on the automobile parts listed in U.S. note 33(g) (9903.94.05), from every country: in Chapter 90, rangefinders (9015.10), revolution counters, production counters and odometers (9029.10) and other speedometers and tachometers (9029.20.40.80), when they are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks. USMCA-qualifying parts and listed articles that are not such parts enter under 9903.94.06.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125% from April 10, 2025, and paused the higher country rates announced on April 2 for other countries, which never took effect. With the 20% fentanyl duty, Chinese syringes (100% under note 31) paid 245% until May 13, 2025, and a patient monitor (List 1) 170%.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) from April 5, 2025, and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 90 product was on the general exemption list, so medical devices paid it; automobile parts paying Section 232 were outside it. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 200% Section 232 duty on Russian aluminum derivatives continued
changes.detail: Proclamation 10895 restored the Section 232 aluminum duty for every country from March 12, 2025 and kept the 200% rate for aluminum products of Russia and for aluminum smelted or cast in Russia (first set by Proclamation 10522). In Chapter 90 it reaches the two lines on the note 19(k) derivative list: other parts of optical appliances (9013.90.80) and parts of measuring instruments (9031.90.91) (9903.85.68).

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the Section 301 duties. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China: 100% on syringes and needles
changes.detail: After the statutory four-year review, USTR raised the Section 301 duty on Chinese syringes and needles of 9018.31 and 9018.32 to 100% (U.S. note 31(d), 9903.91.03). Enteral syringes (9018.31.00.80) were exempt until December 31, 2025 (9903.91.10); since January 1, 2026 they pay the 100% too.

changes.title: China List 4A duty cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: USTR halved the List 4A duty (9903.88.15) from 15% to 7.5% under the Phase One agreement. In Chapter 90 List 4A covers contact and spectacle lenses, frames, sunglasses and goggles, binoculars, most still cameras, and some thermometers and flow instruments.

changes.title: China List 4A reaches lenses, eyewear and cameras
changes.detail: The fourth China Section 301 list put +15% on most Chinese contact and spectacle lenses, frames, sunglasses, binoculars and cameras. Catheters, dental, therapy, respiratory, orthopedic and implant devices were left off the lists and have never been charged.

changes.title: China List 3 duty raised to 25%
changes.detail: USTR raised the List 3 duty (9903.88.03) from 10% to 25%. In Chapter 90 List 3 covers unmounted and mounted optical elements, cinematographic and photo-lab equipment, surveying instruments, balances and drafting and hand measuring instruments.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 reaches optics and measuring tools
changes.detail: The third China Section 301 list put +10% (9903.88.03) on 85 more Chapter 90 lines, mainly optics, photographic and drafting equipment.

changes.title: China List 2 reaches optical fibers and meters
changes.detail: The second China Section 301 list put +25% (9903.88.02) on optical fibers and polarizing sheet (9001.10, 9001.20), some thermometers and pyrometers, gas, liquid and electricity meters, speedometers and multimeters.

changes.title: China List 1 reaches medical imaging and instruments
changes.detail: The first China Section 301 list put +25% (9903.88.01) on 193 of today's Chapter 90 lines: electro-diagnostic, ultrasound, MRI and X-ray apparatus, microscopes, navigational, analytical, electrical test, measuring and inspection instruments, thermostats and regulators.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 90 goods were **$125.68B in 2025**, 0.7% more than the $124.83B of 2024 and up from $90.87B in 2020. **Medical, surgical and dental instruments (heading 9018)** were the largest group at $44.52B — $22.27B of other instruments, $10.36B of catheters and cannulas and $6.31B of electro-diagnostic apparatus — followed by **orthopedic devices, implants and hearing aids (9021)** at $19.41B, **lab analyzers (9027)** at $7.85B, **measuring and inspection instruments (9031)** at $7.25B, **therapy and respiratory apparatus (9019)** at $6.64B and **X-ray and CT (9022)** at $4.78B.

**Mexico** is the largest supplier ($24.14B, up 5.3%), more than half of it medical instruments ($12.94B), largely duty-free under USMCA. **Germany** ($13.53B) leads in X-ray, lab and measuring instruments; **China** fell 17.1% to $10.23B, from $14.11B in 2021; **Ireland** ($9.89B) ships mostly implants and medical instruments ($5.67B of 9021). **Costa Rica** grew 21.9% to $7.09B, mostly medical instruments, from $2.59B in 2020. Japan ($7.09B), Singapore ($4.92B, respiratory apparatus), Canada ($4.82B), Malaysia ($4.41B, electrical test instruments) and Switzerland ($4.39B, implants) follow; Denmark, which ships mainly heading 9021 devices, rose 45.0%.

The figures are annual and stop at 2025, before the 2026 tariff changes (the end of the IEEPA duties in February, the Section 301 tariffs from July 24 and the Canada Section 338 duties from August 22); they do not show what those changes did. Duty-collected figures are not available from an official source yet.

industryAreas.intro:
Chapter 90 base rates are low — every medical, surgical, dental, orthopedic and X-ray line is Free, and most instruments pay Free to about 7% — so the duty you pay **depends almost entirely on where the goods come from**. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — taken from the current tariff schedule.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** that started July 24, 2026: **10% in total for the EU and Taiwan**, **12.5% in total for Japan, Korea and Switzerland**, **+10% for Malaysia, India and the UK**, **+12.5% for Costa Rica, Singapore, Israel and Vietnam**. **China adds 37.5%** on most instruments and imaging equipment, 20% on eyewear and cameras, 12.5% on catheters, implants and other devices that are on no list, and **112.5% on syringes and needles**. USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico and Canada pay nothing, except **50% Section 338 on Canadian optical measuring instruments**. 63 British medical-device lines and 10 semiconductor-equipment lines pay no Section 301 duty. Where a cell shows two or three totals, the line also carries a **Section 232 vehicle-parts duty** (car or light-truck part, truck or bus part) — pick the case that matches the goods. Parts of binoculars and telescopes (9005.90) and of drafting and measuring instruments (9017.90) pay "the rate applicable to the article of which it is a part": the cells show that wording, and the tariff calculator asks for the article's HTS line and prices the part at that line's rate before adding the extra duty.

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
A per-unit rate plus a percentage cannot be added into one number without the shipment’s weight, count or volume, so it is shown as written.

Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; P for Costa Rica; JP for Japan; SG for Singapore; IL for Israel; KR for South Korea. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Conditional relief is not applied when it needs the importer's confirmation: the 9903.88.69 (Section 301) China exclusions defined by a product description, and the civil-aircraft exemptions.
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Multi-total cells: the Section 232 automobile-parts duty applies only to note 33(g) articles (rangefinders 9015.10, counters 9029.10, speedometers 9029.20.40.80) that are parts of passenger vehicles or light trucks, and the medium- and heavy-duty duty only to note 38(i) articles (9029.10.80, 9029.20.40.80) that are parts of trucks, tractors or buses; "car or light-truck part or truck or bus part" is one total for both. "Not a vehicle part" means neither — a listed article for other use enters under 9903.94.06 or 9903.74.11 and pays the base rate plus the Section 301 duty.

"The rate applicable to the article of which it is a part or accessory" (9005.90.40, 9005.90.80, 9017.90.01): the base rate is the rate of the article the part belongs to — for example Free for a prism-binocular part (9005.10), 8% for a telescope part (9005.80.40), 5.8% for a caliper part (9017.30.40). The importer gives that article's HTS line, and the calculator prices the part at that line's rate on the part's full value, then adds the extra duty (for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan the higher of that rate and the 10% or 12.5% floor).

Section 232 metals (9013.90.80): priced at 15% in total, assuming the aluminum is not U.S.-smelted and is at least 15% of the article's weight; goods with no aluminum, steel or copper (9903.82.01) or under 15% metal by weight (9903.82.03) pay the base rate plus the Section 301 duty instead.

Canada, "USMCA-qualifying" side: the Section 301 and vehicle-parts duties are removed (9903.05.93, 9903.94.06, 9903.74.10), but the 50% Section 338 duty stays on 9031.49.90 because U.S. note 51(a) applies it even when a special rate is claimed.
The per-unit rates on gas and liquid meters and stroboscopes (16¢ each + 2.5%) are priced at 1,000 units on a $10,000 shipment for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan "in total" rules.

China exclusions in note 20(vvv) that cover a whole statistical line (9030.90.46; 9025.19.80.10, .20 and .85) are applied in the cells. Not in the cells: the exclusions defined by a product description and the civil-aircraft exemptions (notes 52(d), 50(a)(iv), 51(d)) — they need the importer's confirmation; the Nairobi Protocol (9817.00.96) and other Chapter 98 entries; FTA preferences other than USMCA, CAFTA-DR, KORUS and the Singapore, Israel and Japan agreements; and FDA, FCC or NRC compliance costs. There is no antidumping or countervailing duty order on a Chapter 90 product. The opt-in Section 232 certified-parts headings are not modeled.

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026, and the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; neither is applied. The Section 232 investigation of medical devices has imposed no duty.
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 16, 19, 20, 30, 31, 33, 38, 39, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Section 301 (2026): the general exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86) names 8 Chapter 90 provisions (10 lines) — 9030.82.00, 9030.90.84, 9031.41.00, 9031.49.70, 9031.80.40, 9031.90.45, 9031.90.54 and 9031.90.70, all semiconductor wafer, photomask or reticle measuring and inspection equipment and parts; the particular-articles list (52(c)) and the pharmaceutical list (52(e)) name none; civil aircraft articles (52(d), 9903.05.88) reach 114 lines with a certification. Of the country exception lists in note 52(j), only the UK list (52(j)(1), 9903.05.96) names Chapter 90 provisions — 63 lines of 9018–9022; the EU, Swiss, Malaysian, Taiwanese, Central American and other lists name none. The Brazil list (note 50(a)(ii)) has no Chapter 90 line. The Canada Section 338 list (note 51(b)(3)) names 9031.49.90; the alcoholic-beverage and dairy lists and the September 29, 2026 import bans name none. China: Lists 1, 2, 3 and 4A (note 20) reach 193, 25, 85 and 61 lines; note 31(d) charges 100% on 9018.31 and 9018.32 (the enteral-syringe exception, 9903.91.10, ended December 31, 2025); about 20 product exclusions in note 20(vvv) run through November 9, 2026. Section 232: note 16(c)(ix) lists 9013.90.80 as a derivative aluminum article; note 19(k) lists 9013.90.80 and 9031.90.91 (200% for Russian aluminum); note 33(g) names 9015.10, 9029.10 and 9029.20.40.80 and note 33(j) the same five lines for the UK; note 38(i) names 9029.10.80 and 9029.20.40.80; the semiconductor note 39 names no Chapter 90 line. Note 30(b) sets 35% for eight Russian lines in place of column 2. A Federal Register search of Commerce notices found no antidumping or countervailing duty order on a Chapter 90 product; orders on other products, such as aluminum extrusions from China, can still cover parts entered under Chapter 90 because their written scope controls.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 90: Optical, Medical & Precision Instruments — Import Rules & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Medical Devices & Instruments into the U.S.: FDA Registration, 510(k), Form FDA 2877, Laser & X-ray Rules and Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 90) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What each HTS Chapter 90 line needs at U.S. entry — FDA establishment registration and device listing (21 CFR 807), 510(k) or PMA, radiation-emitting product declarations on Form FDA 2877, impact-resistant eyewear, FCC and NRC rules — and the legal ways to pay less: classification, origin, USMCA, the Nairobi Protocol, China exclusions, first sale, drawback and FTZ.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most Chapter 90 goods enter at low or Free base rates, but many lines carry agency rules. **Medical devices** of headings 9018–9022 — and contact lenses, eyeglasses, sunglasses, frames and clinical thermometers — are FDA-regulated: the foreign maker must **register its establishment and list the device** with FDA and name a U.S. agent, the device must be **510(k)-cleared, PMA-approved or exempt**, and FDA reviews every entry and can refuse admission. **Lasers, X-ray and other radiation-emitting products** under a federal performance standard need a **Form FDA 2877** declaration at entry. Eyeglass and sunglass lenses must be **impact-resistant**, electronic instruments that emit radio frequency must meet **FCC** import conditions, and equipment with radioactive sources needs an **NRC** import license. Every article must be **marked with its country of origin**.

On cost, the levers are the **classification** (parts follow the rules of note 2; a part of a binocular or caliper takes the rate of the article), the **country of origin** (Free from the UK on 63 medical lines, 10% in total from the EU, 112.5% on Chinese syringes), **USMCA**, the **Nairobi Protocol** for articles for persons with disabilities, the **China product exclusions**, the semiconductor-equipment and civil-aircraft exemptions, whether an instrument is in fact a **vehicle part**, the **metal content** of 9013.90.80 parts, and first-sale valuation, drawback and foreign-trade zones. Each lever depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Classify by function, and parts by note 2
levers.saves: The gap between line rates and between China lists: optical fibers 6.7%, mounted camera lenses 2.3%, rifle scopes 14.9%, magnifiers 6.6%, plotters Free, micrometers 5.8%; a Chinese catheter (no list) pays 12.5% extra, a Chinese patient monitor (List 1) 37.5%
levers.appliesTo: All headings; especially parts, which go to their own heading in chapters 84, 85, 90 or 91, then with the article they serve, and only otherwise to 9033 (4.4%)
levers.document: Technical documentation: function, principle of operation, what the part fits and whether it is used solely or principally with one kind of instrument.
levers.caveat: Chapter 90 note 1 sends many goods elsewhere: digital cameras (8525), radar and GPS (8526), optical fiber cables of 8544, semiconductor manufacturing machines (8486), parts of general use (Section XV). The classification must match the goods; a ruling settles doubtful cases.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 90, notes 1–7 and additional U.S. notes

levers.title: Document the article a binocular, telescope or drafting-instrument part belongs to
levers.saves: The difference between article rates: a part of prism binoculars takes Free (9005.10), of an optical telescope 8% (9005.80.40), of a caliper 5.8% (9017.30.40), of a plotter Free (9017.10.40)
levers.appliesTo: 9005.90.40, 9005.90.80 and 9017.90.01, whose rate is "the rate applicable to the article of which it is a part or accessory"
levers.document: Proof of the article the part is for — drawings, the parts list of the finished instrument — and that article's HTS line.
levers.caveat: The part pays the rate of the article's line on the part's own value; the extra duty by country is added as for any other line, and China's List 4A or List 3 duty applies to the part's own line.

levers.title: Know the country of origin and the country's exception lists
levers.saves: The difference between country rates: nothing on 63 British medical lines, 10% in total from the EU, +10% from Malaysia or India, +12.5% from Costa Rica or Singapore, +12.5% to +112.5% from China
levers.appliesTo: All lines; the gap is widest on Chinese syringes, imaging and measuring instruments
levers.document: Production records showing where the device was made or substantially transformed — for a medical device often where the finished device was assembled, sterilized or calibrated — consistent with the FDA listing.
levers.caveat: Final packing, sterilization or labeling alone does not usually change origin; CBP decides by substantial transformation and can ask for proof. The UK exception list covers only the 63 lines it names, and only goods that are products of the UK.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 31, 51, 52(j)

levers.title: Claim USMCA on devices and instruments from Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate, the 10% Section 301 duty and the 25% Section 232 vehicle-parts duty
levers.appliesTo: All lines from Mexico — the largest Chapter 90 supplier — and Canada (except 9031.49.90 from Canada, which keeps the 50% Section 338 duty)
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, kept ready for CBP.
levers.caveat: The good must meet the Chapter 90 rule of origin in General Note 11 for its subheading. USMCA does not remove the Section 232 metals duty on 9013.90.80 or the Canada Section 338 duty. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: HTSUS General Note 11 (USMCA rules of origin)

levers.title: Claim AGOA, CBERA or another FTA on dutiable lines
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 16%) on the dutiable lines
levers.appliesTo: Dutiable lines whose Special column lists the program: AGOA (D), CBERA (E), CAFTA-DR (P), Israel (IL), Singapore (SG), Korea (KR), Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru and the other FTA partners
levers.document: The origin proof each program requires (a certification or declaration of origin) and records to back it up.
levers.caveat: An FTA removes the base rate but not the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)) — a Costa Rican, Israeli or Singaporean device pays 12.5% even when the base rate is Free, a Korean one 12.5% in total. AGOA (D) runs to December 31, 2026. GSP (A, A*, A+) has been expired since December 31, 2020, although the codes are still printed.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Enter articles for persons with disabilities under 9817.00.96
levers.saves: The base rate and the Section 301 (2026 and China) and Canada Section 338 duties, which do not apply to goods properly entered under Chapter 98 (other than 9802 and subchapter XXIII)
levers.appliesTo: Articles specially designed or adapted for the use or benefit of persons with a permanent or chronic physical or mental impairment — for example some orthopedic and prosthetic devices and hearing aids of heading 9021
levers.document: Evidence of the special design or adaptation and the intended users, as CBP requires for the provision.
levers.caveat: U.S. note 4(b) to Chapter 98 subchapter XVII excludes articles for acute or transient disability, spectacles and cosmetic articles for people not substantially disabled, therapeutic and diagnostic articles, and medicine — so most of heading 9018 does not qualify. Section 232 duties still apply.

citations.label: HTSUS Chapter 98, subchapter XVII, U.S. note 4, 9817.00.96
HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 31, 51(a), 52(a)

levers.title: Use a China Section 301 exclusion for qualifying goods
levers.saves: The 25% List 1, 2 or 3 duty or the 7.5% List 4A duty on Chinese goods that match an exclusion description
levers.appliesTo: About 20 items, including ECG electrodes, portable ultrasonic scanners, professional blood-pressure monitors, peak-flow meters and pulse oximeters, anesthesia instruments, cautery pencils, PET/CT scanners, radiotherapy systems, X-ray tube housings, multi-leaf collimators, certain thermometers and gas monitors, protective goggles, prism binoculars, weather station sets and wall thermostats
levers.document: Product specifications showing the goods match the description in note 20(vvv); report 9903.88.69 instead of the list heading.
levers.caveat: In effect through November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends them again. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty still applies, and the 100% duty on syringes and needles has no exclusion.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 20(vvv), 9903.88.69

levers.title: Check the semiconductor-equipment exemption from the 2026 Section 301 duty
levers.saves: The 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty (or the EU, Japan, Korea, Swiss or Taiwan floor) on measuring and inspection equipment for semiconductor wafers, photomasks and reticles
levers.document: Specifications showing the instrument is for measuring or inspecting semiconductor wafers or devices, photomasks or reticles, so that it is correctly classified in one of the listed provisions.
levers.caveat: Only the listed provisions qualify; general-purpose measuring instruments do not. China's List 1 duty still applies.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(b), 9903.05.86

levers.title: Certify civil aircraft instruments
levers.saves: The 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty and the Brazil duty on instruments and parts for civil aircraft
levers.appliesTo: 114 Chapter 90 lines named in note 52(d), among them aircraft compasses, autopilots, navigational instruments, thermometers, flow and pressure gauges, speedometers, electrical test instruments and regulators
levers.document: The civil aircraft certification CBP requires (entry under 9903.05.88; 9903.05.05 for Brazil).
levers.caveat: Military aircraft are excluded. China's list duties still apply.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 50(a)(iv), 52(d)

levers.title: Document whether rangefinders, counters and speedometers are vehicle parts
levers.saves: The 25% Section 232 duty (or the 15% / 10% deal rates) on listed instruments that are not parts of passenger vehicles, light trucks or medium- and heavy-duty vehicles
levers.document: Evidence of the end use — the vehicle model, customer and application — to support entry under 9903.94.06 or 9903.74.11 instead of 9903.94.05 or 9903.74.08.
levers.caveat: Only articles that are really not parts of those vehicles qualify; CBP's FAQs explain how to report them. A part that does pay Section 232 is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty, so the saving is the difference, not the full 25%.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 33(g)–(h), 38(i)–(l)
CBP Section 232 FAQs: automobiles and automobile parts

levers.title: Show the metal content of 9013.90.80 optical parts
levers.saves: The 15%-in-total Section 232 metals duty — down to 10% in total with U.S.-smelted aluminum, or none if the part has no aluminum, steel or copper or the metal is under 15% of its weight
levers.appliesTo: 9013.90.80.00 (other parts and accessories of lasers and other optical appliances)
levers.document: A bill of materials with metal weights and, for the 10% rate, mill certificates showing at least 85% of the aluminum was smelted and cast in the United States.
levers.caveat: Without the metals duty the part pays its 4.5% base rate plus the Section 301 duty. The temporary 15% rate ends December 31, 2027.

levers.title: Value at the first sale for export when you buy through a middleman
levers.saves: Every ad valorem duty is charged on a lower value — the 10%–112.5% extra duties included — when the factory price to a trading company is lower than the price you pay
levers.appliesTo: All lines with ad valorem duties bought through a trading company or distributor rather than straight from the maker
levers.document: Proof that the first sale was a bona fide sale for export to the United States at arm's length: the factory invoice, contracts and payment records.
levers.caveat: Only a sale clearly destined for the U.S. qualifies, and the importer must be able to show the earlier price at entry. Related-party prices must meet the transaction-value tests.

levers.title: Recover duty on goods you export or destroy
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, when the imported goods (or goods made from them) are exported or destroyed
levers.appliesTo: Any line — for example components built into instruments or devices that are then exported
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import, manufacturing and export records.
levers.caveat: Claims have filing deadlines and record-keeping rules; antidumping and countervailing duties are not refunded by drawback.

levers.title: Process or hold devices in a foreign-trade zone
levers.saves: No duty on goods re-exported from the zone, and duty deferred until goods leave it for the U.S. market
levers.appliesTo: Any line — useful for device and instrument makers that assemble from imported components and export part of output
levers.document: Zone admission (CBP Form 214) and the zone operator's inventory records.
levers.caveat: Goods entered for U.S. consumption from a zone pay the duties in force on the entry date; goods subject to Section 232 or the China Section 301 duties must be admitted in privileged foreign status, so the zone does not lower those duties.

levers.title: Use Chapter 98 for U.S. goods returned or repaired abroad
levers.saves: All duty on U.S.-made instruments returned unchanged (9801.00.10); on goods repaired abroad (9802.00.40/.50), duty only on the value of the repair
levers.appliesTo: Any line — for example U.S.-made medical or test equipment sent abroad for repair or calibration and returned
levers.document: Proof of U.S. origin and of the export, and repair invoices, as CBP requires for each provision.
levers.caveat: The Section 301 duties apply only to the value of the repair under 9802.00.40/.50 and do not apply to most other Chapter 98 entries (U.S. notes 20, 51(a), 52(a)).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20, 51(a), 52(a)

levers.title: Get a binding classification ruling
levers.saves: Certainty where the line decides the rate and the extra duty: a part of a medical device (9018.90) versus a part of general use; an instrument of 9027 versus 9031; a lab analyzer that is a medical device; whether a part is "for" binoculars or telescopes
levers.appliesTo: Any line where function, construction or use decides the line
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing the article, its function, materials, value and use.
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a changed design may need a new one.

rules.title: Medical devices: the foreign manufacturer must register its establishment and list each device with FDA, and name a U.S. agent; no device may be imported unless it is listed and made at a registered establishment (investigational devices aside)
Medical devices must be 510(k)-cleared, PMA-approved or exempt before commercial distribution, and made under the quality management system regulation

FDA reviews device entries (product code, registration and listing, affirmations of compliance) and can detain and refuse admission to devices that appear adulterated or misbranded; labels must name the manufacturer, packer or distributor

Radiation-emitting electronic products under a federal performance standard — lasers and laser products, diagnostic X-ray systems — must be certified and labeled, and need a Form FDA 2877 declaration at entry; noncomplying products are refused or brought into compliance under bond

citations.label: FDA: Importing Radiation-Emitting Electronic Products (Form FDA 2877)

rules.title: Eyeglasses and sunglasses must have impact-resistant lenses, tested by the manufacturer (the drop-ball test or an equal or superior one)
Over-the-counter hearing aids must meet FDA's OTC hearing aid labeling, output and design requirements
Electronic instruments that are radio-frequency devices (digital electronics, wireless sensors and monitors) may be imported only if authorized or otherwise eligible under the FCC import conditions

Equipment containing radioactive (byproduct) material — some radiation-based gauges and therapy apparatus, ionization smoke detectors — may be imported under the general license only by a consignee authorized to possess the material
Country-of-origin marking in English, legible, indelible and permanent enough to reach the ultimate purchaser — on the article or, where allowed, its container

No antidumping or countervailing duty order covers a Chapter 90 product, but orders on other goods apply by their written scope whatever the HTS line — for example aluminum extrusions from China entered as parts of instruments

citations.label: 76 FR 30650 (aluminum extrusions order: scope covers extrusions entered under other chapters)

rules.title: Report the Chapter 99 headings with the line: the 2026 Section 301 heading for the country or its exemption (9903.05.86, .88, .96), China Lists 1–4A (9903.88.01–.03, .15), the 2024 increase (9903.91.03) or an exclusion (9903.88.69), Section 232 vehicle parts (9903.94.05/.06, 9903.74.08/.10/.11) or metals (9903.82.xx), Canada Section 338 (9903.03.14)

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 16, 20, 30, 31, 33, 38, 50–52

groups.label: Optical fibers, contact lenses, spectacle lenses & unmounted optics
groups.note: Contact lenses and spectacle lenses are FDA-regulated devices; lenses for eyeglasses and sunglasses must be impact-resistant. Optical fibers are on China List 2 (+25%), contact and spectacle lenses on List 4A (+7.5%).

groups.label: Mounted lenses, filters, prisms & mirrors for instruments
groups.note: Mounted lenses and filters are parts of instruments; CCTV lenses entered separately are classified here, not with the camera.

groups.label: Eyeglass frames & parts
groups.note: Spectacle frames are FDA-regulated devices: the foreign maker must register and list them. China List 4A (+7.5%).

groups.label: Sunglasses, safety glasses & goggles
groups.note: Sunglasses and eyeglasses are FDA devices and need impact-resistant lenses. Chinese protective goggles of 9004.90 may match a List 4A exclusion through November 9, 2026.

groups.label: Binoculars, telescopes & astronomical instruments
groups.note: Parts of 9005.90 take the rate of the binocular or telescope they belong to; give that article's HTS line. Prism binoculars of a listed size are excluded from List 4A.

groups.label: Still cameras, flash units & parts
groups.note: Digital cameras are classified in 8525, not here. Cheap cameras ($10 or less) pay 6.8%.

groups.label: Cinematographic cameras & projectors
groups.note: No agency license for cine cameras and projectors.

groups.label: Image projectors, enlargers & reducers
groups.note: Video and data projectors are heading 8528; slide and overhead projectors are here.

groups.label: Photo lab equipment, negatoscopes & projection screens
groups.note: No agency license for photo-lab apparatus and projection screens.

groups.label: Optical microscopes
groups.note: No agency license for optical microscopes; Chinese microscopes are on List 1 or 3 (+25%).

groups.label: Electron microscopes & diffraction apparatus
groups.note: Electron microscopes are on China List 1 (+25%).

groups.label: Lasers, rifle scopes, magnifiers & other optical devices
groups.note: Laser products must meet the FDA laser performance standard and carry a Form FDA 2877 declaration at entry. 9013.90.80 parts pay the Section 232 metals duty (15% in total) unless they contain no metal or under 15% by weight.

groups.label: Compasses, autopilots & navigational instruments
groups.note: Aircraft compasses, autopilots and navigational instruments can use the civil aircraft exemptions with a certification.

groups.label: Surveying, rangefinders, weather & geophysical instruments
groups.note: Laser rangefinders and laser levels are laser products under the FDA standard. Rangefinders (9015.10) that are car parts pay the Section 232 auto-parts duty.

groups.label: Precision balances (5 cg or better)
groups.note: No agency license for precision balances.

groups.label: Drafting instruments, calipers, micrometers & measuring tapes
groups.note: Parts of 9017.90 take the rate of the instrument they belong to; give that article's HTS line.

groups.label: Medical, surgical, dental & veterinary instruments (incl. syringes, catheters, ECG, ultrasound, MRI)
groups.note: FDA-regulated medical devices: registration and listing, 510(k) or PMA, and FDA entry review. Chinese syringes and needles (9018.31, 9018.32) pay 100% more under Section 301; ECG electrodes, ultrasound scanners, professional blood-pressure monitors and anesthesia instruments may match a China exclusion. 9018 is part of the open Section 232 medical-device investigation.

groups.label: Massage & mechano-therapy apparatus, oxygen therapy, ventilators & CPAP
groups.note: Ventilators, CPAP, oxygen and aerosol therapy apparatus are FDA devices; on no China list (12.5% only).

groups.label: Breathing appliances & gas masks
groups.note: Gas masks and breathing appliances pay 2.5%; breathing devices for medical use can also be FDA devices. Underwater breathing devices are Free.

groups.label: Orthopedic devices, implants, artificial joints, hearing aids & pacemakers
groups.note: Implants, prostheses, hearing aids and pacemakers are FDA devices (OTC hearing aids under 21 CFR 800.30). Articles for persons with a chronic disability may qualify for the Nairobi Protocol (9817.00.96). British artificial joints, hearing aids and pacemakers pay no Section 301 duty.

groups.label: X-ray, CT & radiotherapy apparatus and X-ray tubes
groups.note: Diagnostic X-ray systems must meet the FDA X-ray performance standard (Form FDA 2877); apparatus with radioactive sources needs an NRC-authorized consignee. PET/CT scanners, radiotherapy systems and X-ray tube housings may match a China exclusion.

groups.label: Demonstration instruments & models
groups.note: No agency license for demonstration models; China List 4A (+7.5%).

groups.label: Materials-testing machines (hardness, strength)
groups.note: No agency license for materials-testing machines; China List 1 (+25%).

groups.label: Thermometers, pyrometers, barometers, hydrometers & hygrometers
groups.note: Clinical thermometers are FDA devices; certain thermometers of 9025.19.80 are excluded from China List 2 through November 9, 2026.

groups.label: Flow meters, level gauges & pressure instruments
groups.note: Aircraft flow and pressure instruments can use the civil aircraft exemptions with a certification.

groups.label: Laboratory analysis instruments: spectrometers, chromatographs, analyzers
groups.note: Lab analyzers used for clinical diagnosis can be FDA in-vitro diagnostic devices. Portable gas monitors may match a China exclusion.

groups.label: Gas, liquid & electricity supply meters
groups.note: Gas and liquid meters pay a per-unit rate (16¢ each + 2.5%).

groups.label: Counters, taximeters, speedometers & tachometers
groups.note: Speedometers and counters that are car, truck or bus parts pay the Section 232 vehicle-parts duty.

groups.label: Oscilloscopes, multimeters, electrical test & radiation-measuring instruments
groups.note: Semiconductor-wafer testers (9030.82) and their parts are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty.

groups.label: Measuring & inspection machines: CMMs, wafer and mask inspection, test benches
groups.note: Wafer, photomask and reticle inspection equipment is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty (note 52(b)); Canadian optical measuring instruments of 9031.49.90 pay 50% Section 338 even under USMCA.

groups.label: Thermostats, manostats & automatic regulating instruments
groups.note: Thermostats and regulators are on China List 1 (+25%); wall thermostats not connected to the internet may match an exclusion.

groups.label: Parts & accessories not specified elsewhere in Chapter 90
groups.note: Only parts not classifiable elsewhere in the chapter or in chapters 84, 85 or 91 go here (Chapter 90 note 2).

tariffEngineering.disclaimer: A checklist of where the rules are, with links to the regulations and the tariff schedule — not legal or regulatory advice. Which line an instrument or device falls in, whether it is FDA-regulated, a vehicle part or covered by an exclusion, and which Chapter 99 duties apply depend on the facts of each shipment, and the extra duties change by Federal Register notice and CBP guidance; confirm the current headings, rates and FDA requirements before each shipment.

seo.title: Medical Device Tariff FAQ: Section 232, China, Syringes, Hearing Aids, Eyeglasses & HS Codes 9018, 9021, 9027, 9031 (HTS Ch. 90) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. tariffs on medical devices and instruments: whether medical devices are exempt, the Section 232 medical-device investigation, Chinese syringes and medical equipment, hearing aids, eyeglasses and sunglasses, and the HS codes for medical devices, thermometers, lab and measuring instruments.
keywords: are medical devices exempt from tariffs
tariffs on medical devices from china

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about U.S. tariffs and import rules for medical devices, optical, measuring and precision instruments. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: 308 of the 421 Chapter 90 lines are Free, including every medical, surgical, dental, orthopedic and X-ray line; the dutiable optical and measuring lines pay mostly 1%–7%.

Since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 duty is added by country: 10% in total for the EU and Taiwan, 12.5% for Japan, Korea and Switzerland, +10% for Malaysia, India and the UK, +12.5% for Costa Rica, Singapore, Israel and Vietnam. 63 British medical lines and 10 semiconductor-equipment lines are exempt.

China pays +37.5% on most instruments and imaging equipment (Lists 1–3), +20% on lenses, eyewear, binoculars and cameras (List 4A), +112.5% on syringes and needles, and +12.5% on catheters, implants, hearing aids and other devices on no list.
USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico — the largest supplier — and Canada pay nothing, except Canadian optical measuring instruments of 9031.49.90 (50% Section 338).

Section 232 reaches only a few lines today: rangefinders, counters and speedometers that are vehicle parts, and 9013.90.80 optical parts (15% in total). The Section 232 medical-device investigation opened in September 2025 has imposed no duty.

The IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026 and the 10% Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026. Medical devices need FDA registration, listing and clearance; lasers and X-ray equipment a Form FDA 2877 declaration.
