faqs.question: Are there tariffs on medical devices imported into the U.S.?
searchedAs: us tariffs on medical devices from india
faqs.answer: The base rate on medical, surgical, dental and orthopedic devices is Free, but most countries pay an extra duty. Since July 24, 2026 the Section 301 tariff adds 10% in total for EU goods, 12.5% in total for Japan, Korea and Switzerland, +10% for India, Malaysia and the UK, +12.5% for Costa Rica, Singapore and Israel, and +12.5% to +112.5% for China. USMCA-qualifying devices from Mexico and Canada pay nothing, and 63 British medical lines are exempt.

faqs.question: Are medical devices exempt from tariffs?
searchedAs: are medical devices exempt from tariffs
are medical devices exempt from us tariffs
are medical supplies exempt from tariffs
faqs.answer: Only partly. The base rate is Free, but there is no general exemption from the 2026 Section 301 tariff for medical devices: the general exemption list (note 52(b)) names only semiconductor test and inspection equipment in Chapter 90. Exempt are British goods on the UK list (63 lines of 9018–9022), USMCA-qualifying goods from Mexico and Canada, civil aircraft instruments, and articles for persons with a chronic disability properly entered under 9817.00.96 (diagnostic and therapeutic articles excluded).

faqs.question: Is there a Section 232 tariff on medical devices?
faqs.answer: Not yet. Commerce opened a Section 232 investigation into PPE, medical consumables and medical equipment and devices on September 2, 2025 (comments were due October 17, 2025), but as of October 13, 2026 no proclamation has imposed a duty under it. The only Section 232 duties in Chapter 90 today are on rangefinders, counters and speedometers that are vehicle parts and on 9013.90.80 optical parts (metals, 15% in total).

faqs.question: What are the tariffs on medical devices from China?
searchedAs: tariffs on medical devices from china
tariff on medical equipment from china
tariffs on medical supplies from china
faqs.answer: Chinese Chapter 90 goods pay the base rate plus 12.5% (2026 Section 301, 9903.05.31), plus 25% on List 1–3 lines — most electro-diagnostic, ultrasound, MRI and X-ray apparatus and lab and measuring instruments — so 37.5%; plus 100% on syringes and needles (112.5%). Catheters, dental, therapy and respiratory devices, most implants and hearing aids are on no list and pay 12.5%. About 20 products are excluded from the list duties through November 9, 2026. China supplied $10.23B in 2025, 17.1% less than in 2024.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for syringes and needles?
faqs.answer: Syringes, with or without needles, are 9018.31 (hypodermic 9018.31.00.40, other 9018.31.00.80, parts .90) and tubular metal needles and suture needles 9018.32 — all Free. From China they pay 112.5% (12.5% plus the 100% 2024 Section 301 increase, which has no exclusion); from the EU 10% in total, from India or Malaysia 10%, from Mexico under USMCA nothing.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for medical devices?
faqs.answer: Most medical devices are in Chapter 90: 9018 for medical, surgical, dental and veterinary instruments (9018.11–9018.19 electro-diagnostic apparatus such as ECG, ultrasound, MRI and patient monitors; 9018.31–9018.39 syringes, needles and catheters; 9018.41–9018.49 dental; 9018.50 ophthalmic; 9018.90 other instruments); 9019 therapy and respiratory apparatus; 9021 orthopedic devices, implants and hearing aids; 9022 X-ray and CT. All are Free before the extra duty by country.

faqs.question: What is HS code 9021 (orthopedic devices and implants)?
faqs.answer: Heading 9021 covers orthopedic appliances and fracture devices including bone plates and screws (9021.10), artificial teeth and dental fittings (9021.21–9021.29), artificial joints (9021.31) and other artificial body parts such as heart valves (9021.39), hearing aids (9021.40), pacemakers (9021.50) and other implanted or worn devices and parts (9021.90). All are Free. Chinese ones pay 12.5% (only pacemakers are on a China list: 37.5%); EU ones 10% in total; British artificial joints, prostheses, hearing aids and pacemakers nothing.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on hearing aids?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on hearing aids
hs code for hearing aid parts
faqs.answer: Hearing aids are 9021.40 and their parts 9021.90.40 — both Free. The extra duty depends on origin: 10% in total from Denmark, Germany or other EU countries, 12.5% in total from Switzerland, +12.5% from Singapore or China, nothing from the UK (exception list) or USMCA-qualifying Mexico and Canada. Hearing aids specially designed for persons with a chronic hearing impairment may also qualify for 9817.00.96.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on eyeglasses, sunglasses and contact lenses?
faqs.answer: Sunglasses are 9004.10 (2%), safety glasses, goggles and other spectacles 9004.90 (2.5%), plastic frames 9003.11 (2.5%), contact lenses 9001.30 and spectacle lenses 9001.40/.50 (2%). Chinese eyewear adds 12.5% plus 7.5% (List 4A): sunglasses 22%. From Italy or France 10% in total, from Vietnam 14.5%. Eyeglass and sunglass lenses must be impact-resistant under FDA rules.

faqs.question: What is HS code 9027?
faqs.answer: Heading 9027 covers instruments for physical or chemical analysis: gas and smoke analyzers (9027.10), chromatographs and electrophoresis instruments (9027.20), spectrometers (9027.30), instruments using optical radiation (9027.50), mass spectrometers (9027.81), other analyzers such as pH and particle instruments (9027.89) and microtomes and parts (9027.90). Almost all are Free (exposure meters 1.2%); Chinese ones pay 37.5% (most on List 1).

faqs.question: What is HS code 9031?
faqs.answer: Heading 9031 covers measuring and checking instruments not elsewhere specified: balancing machines (9031.10), test benches (9031.20, 1.7%), optical inspection of semiconductor wafers, photomasks and reticles (9031.41), coordinate-measuring machines and other optical instruments (9031.49), other instruments and sensors (9031.80) and parts (9031.90). Wafer and mask inspection lines are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty; Canadian 9031.49.90 instruments pay 50% Section 338.

faqs.question: What are HS codes 9026 and 9032?
faqs.answer: 9026 covers instruments for measuring flow, level and pressure of liquids and gases — flow meters (9026.10), pressure gauges and transmitters (9026.20), heat meters and others (9026.80) — all Free. 9032 covers automatic regulating instruments: thermostats (9032.10, 1.7%), manostats (9032.20), hydraulic and pneumatic regulators (9032.81) and other controllers (9032.89, 1.1%–1.7%). Chinese ones pay 37.5% or more (List 1).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for thermometers?
faqs.answer: Thermometers are heading 9025: liquid-filled clinical (9025.11.20) and other (9025.11.40) thermometers, and other thermometers and pyrometers including digital and infrared ones (9025.19) — all Free. Clinical thermometers are FDA devices. From China, liquid thermometers pay 12.5%, and so do the 9025.19.80 statistical lines excluded from List 2 through November 9, 2026 (.10, .20, .85); pyrometers and the other infrared thermometers (9025.19.80.60) pay 37.5%.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for X-ray machines and blood pressure monitors?
searchedAs: hs code for x ray machine parts
hs code for blood pressure monitor
hs code for blood pressure machine
faqs.answer: X-ray apparatus is 9022: CT scanners 9022.12, dental X-ray 9022.13, other medical X-ray 9022.14, industrial and baggage X-ray 9022.19, X-ray tubes 9022.30, parts 9022.90 (Free–1.4%). Blood pressure monitors are 9018.19.95 (electronic) or 9018.90.50 (sphygmomanometers) — Free. Diagnostic X-ray systems need a Form FDA 2877 declaration at entry.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 90 cover?
faqs.answer: HTS Chapter 90 has 421 tariff lines in 32 headings: optical elements, fibers and lenses (9001–9002), eyewear (9003–9004), binoculars, cameras, projectors and microscopes (9005–9013), navigation, surveying and drafting instruments (9014–9017), medical, dental, therapy, orthopedic and X-ray apparatus (9018–9022), testing and measuring instruments, thermometers, meters and controls (9023–9032) and other parts (9033). Clocks and watches are Chapter 91; digital cameras and radar are Chapter 85.
